about: Hilda is named for Konstantin Frank’s daughter, remembered by the family for her work ethic and unrelenting commitment to them. It belongs to the winery’s HELM series, created in 2015 to honor the women of Dr. Frank. Konstantin Frank, a Ukrainian viticulturist, planted vinifera on the west shore of Keuka Lake in 1958, and the family winery he opened in 1962 helped prove that Chardonnay and other European grapes could thrive in New York.

The fruit for Hilda comes from the Eric Volz Vineyard, across the road from the Frank plantings on Keuka Lake. It was planted in 1985 by Walter Volz, the winery’s first vineyard manager, and is tended today by his son Eric, the current vineyard manager. Shallow, shale-heavy soils give high natural acidity. The 2021 was fully barrel fermented in French and acacia barrels, 17% new, with weekly lees stirring and no malolactic fermentation, then aged nine months in barrel. Just 145 cases were made.

A mild winter and a cooler, more typical growing season set up the 2021. The winery describes it as fruity and floral, with white flowers from the acacia barrels, citrus zest and fresh red apple, and a round, generous palate given richness by the oak and creaminess by the lees stirring, ending on a hint of spice.
